ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, points A, B, C, and D are all on the circle \( \odot O\), with \( OA\perp BC\), and \( \angle CDA=25^\circ\). What is the degree measure of \( \angle AOB\)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}\\
Since $ AO\perp BC$\\
It follows that $\overset{\frown}{AC}=\overset{\frown}{AB}$\\
Since $\angle CDA=25^\circ$\\
Thus, $\angle AOB=2\angle CDA=50^\circ$\\
Therefore, the answer is: $\boxed{50^\circ}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure there is a circle with O as the center, A is above the circle, B is at the upper right, C is at the upper left, D is at the lower left, and A, B, C, D are all located on the circumference. The radii OA and OB are drawn in the figure, chord BC is approximately horizontal, OA is approximately vertical and perpendicular to BC; CD and DA are also drawn, so ∠CDA is an inscribed angle formed by DC and DA. Reasoning: Because OA passes through the circle center O and is perpendicular to chord BC, OA bisects the arc subtended by chord BC, in particular A is on arc BC, so arc AB equals arc AC. It is known that ∠CDA = 25°, and what it subtends is arc CA, so the measure of arc CA is 2 × 25° = 50°. Therefore arc AB is also 50°. The central angle ∠AOB subtends arc AB, so ∠AOB = 50°.
